raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 with an EAGLE3 draft does not start on CUDA: TARGET_VERIFY reaches the sparse layers' `forward_extend`, which needs the `extend_seq_lens` that verify batches lack, so the warm-up fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'device'`. #41497 fixed ROCm by verifying a linear draft chain with the sparse decode kernels, one causal row per draft token, but every gate it added is `is_hip`. This PR covers TP, not DP attention.

## Modifications

- Run the #41497 linear-verify path on every non-NPU GPU: `forward_extend` hands verify to `forward_decode` on a shallow copy, one row per draft token, so the dense layers keep their per-request metadata and the draft KV is stored once. `_init_rocm_linear_verify_metadata` becomes `_init_linear_verify_metadata`; the ROCm test only follows the rename.
- On CUDA, accept only EAGLE chains (`topk == 1`) via the existing `draft_is_chain_layout`; tree drafts and other algorithms raise `NotImplementedError` at startup. ROCm keeps its rule: any draft with `topk == 1`.
- Refuse HiSparse with speculative decoding at startup: its swap-in keeps one device buffer and one LRU slot set per request, while verify scores `bs × ndt` rows.
- Bound verify capture by the context length on every platform (CUDA capture took the bound from the 1-token dummy lengths, a one-column score buffer that `_decode_score_kernel` overruns at replay); the eager bound counts the draft rows.
- Clamp rows past the context length to it, which keeps the verify bound at the context length instead of `context + ndt`: those rows predict positions that are never committed (the scheduler caps `max_new_tokens` below the context length and trims over-accepted drafts), and at 1M context the decode top-k stays in its 8192 register bucket.
- Keep verify rows on Triton when MSA decode is on, since its plan covers decode batches only; MSA with the decode graph and speculative decoding is still refused at startup.

## Accuracy Tests

MiniMax-M3-NVFP4, 4x GB300, TP4, 1M context, thinking enabled, `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA=1`, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935` + this patch; EAGLE3 `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA` (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens, unquantized draft), real verification.

| same build, one tray each | no spec | EAGLE3 |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K 1319 q (5-shot) | 0.861 | **0.864** |
| GSM8K 40 q at `--parallel 1` (bs=1 decode graph) | 0.800 | 0.875 |
| passkey at 131K / 524K / 990K tokens | pass | pass |
| mean acceptance length (GSM8K / long context) | – | 2.81 / 2.90 |

- New `test_minimax_linear_verify.py` (CUDA, H100 and B200 CI; MSA decode on, so verify must stay on Triton) compares verify rows with the same rows decoded alone: eager at prefixes 1000 and 5118 (crosses a block boundary) is bit-exact; a graph captured on 1-token dummies, replayed with one request two tokens short of a 64K context, matches inside the context and clamps rows past it.
- On GB300, dropping the eager draft-token term fails the eager cases and dropping the clamp fails the replay cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Mean TPOT at bs=1 (prompt cached, 256 output tokens, real acceptance), same build, one GB300 tray per arm:

| prompt tokens | no spec | EAGLE3 | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K | 4.34 ms | 2.23 ms | 1.95x |
| 131K | 6.00 ms | 3.40 ms | 1.76x |
| 524K | 9.78 ms | 5.43 ms | 1.80x |
| 990K | 13.88 ms | 8.30 ms | 1.67x |

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server, on `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935` with this PR, 4× GB300 (the no-spec arm drops the `--speculative-*` flags):

```
SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code --tp 4 --context-length 1048576 --reasoning-parser minimax-m3 --tool-call-parser minimax-m3 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"thinking_mode":"enabled"}' --enable-metrics --random-seed 42 --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 --speculative-draft-model-path Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant
```

GSM8K (5-shot): `python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 5 --num-questions 1319`, and `--num-questions 40 --parallel 1` for the bs=1 row.

Passkey: one chat request per size whose prompt is filler text with a random 5-digit key at two thirds depth, sized to 131K / 524K / 990K tokens with the server's chat template; pass when the key is in the answer. bs=1 TPOT: on the same server, a follow-up "count upward" turn on that cached conversation, 256 tokens with `ignore_eos`; the 8K row warms an 8K prefix first.
</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: style | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

The Accuracy Tests and Speed Tests sections give the model, GPUs, TP, image, and EAGLE3 settings, but no commands. Others cannot rerun the GSM8K, passkey, or TPOT numbers.

**Fix**

Add the exact server launch commands for the no-spec and EAGLE3 arms, the GSM8K and passkey eval commands, and the benchmark command behind the bs=1 TPOT table, including input/output lengths and how the prompt was cached.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This line turns on linear verify for CUDA, where the M3 cookbook documents HiSparse. `validate_hisparse` allows HiSparse with `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`, so HiSparse + EAGLE3 now starts. Verify then calls `swap_in_selected_blocks` with `bs * ndt` rows. But `num_real_reqs` holds `batch_size`, and `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` writes `-1` for every row at or past it.

**Example**

With bs=2 and ndt=4, rows 2-7 get no KV slots. The `ndt` rows of one request also update the same `lru_slots[rid]` at the same time. And `top_k_device_locs_buffer` has only one row per request slot.

**Fix**

Raise `NotImplementedError` here when `self.hisparse_coordinator is not None` and speculative decoding is on, until the swap-in handles verify rows.

**Issue**

With this change, verify rows no longer reach MSA or the prefill metadata. The startup guard at lines 298-309 still says MSA + spec + CUDA graph fails because "TARGET_VERIFY batches route to forward_extend, dereferencing absent extend metadata". That is no longer true after this PR. The guard still makes Blackwell EAGLE3 users set `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA=1`, which also turns off MSA for prefill.

**Fix**

Update the comment to give the reason the guard is still needed. If no reason remains, drop the guard so MSA can serve prefill with EAGLE3.

+    minimax_sparse_decode,
+)
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_batch_info import ForwardMode
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+# One TP4 rank of MiniMax-M3: 16 query heads, 1 KV head, 1 index head.
+NQH, NKH, NIH, HD = 16, 1, 1, 128
+BLK, TOPK, INIT_BLOCKS, LOCAL_BLOCKS, PAGE = 128, 16, 0, 1, 128
+NDT = 4
+MAX_CONTEXT = 64 * 1024
+# ReqToTokenPool width with speculative decoding: context + 4 + ndt.
+WIDTH = MAX_CONTEXT + 4 + NDT
+LAYER_ID = 3
+
+
+def _paged_req_to_token(num_reqs, first_page=0):
+    pages_per_req = (WIDTH + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    rows = []
+    for r in range(num_reqs):
+        base = first_page + r * pages_per_req
+        pages = torch.randperm(pages_per_req, device="cuda") + base
+        slots = pages[:, None] * PAGE + torch.arange(PAGE, device="cuda")
+        rows.append(slots.reshape(-1)[:WIDTH])
+    return torch.stack(rows).to(torch.int32), first_page + num_reqs * pages_per_req
+
+
+def _caches(num_slots, with_value):
+    nan = float("nan")
+    k = torch.full((num_slots, NKH, HD), nan, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    v = torch.full_like(k, nan)
+    idx_k = torch.full((num_slots, 1, HD), nan, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    idx_v = torch.full_like(idx_k, nan) if with_value else None
+    return k, v, idx_k, idx_v
+
+
+class _Pool:
+    """The slice of MiniMaxSparseKVPool that forward_decode touches."""
+
+    def __init__(self, k, v, idx_k, idx_v):
+        self.k, self.v, self.idx_k, self.idx_v = k, v, idx_k, idx_v
+
+    def set_fused_kv_index_buffer(self, layer, loc, k, v, idx_k, idx_v, *scales):
+        self.k[loc] = k.view(-1, *self.k.shape[1:])
+        self.v[loc] = v.view(-1, *self.v.shape[1:])
+        self.idx_k[loc] = idx_k.view(-1, *self.idx_k.shape[1:])
+        if idx_v is not None:
+            self.idx_v[loc] = idx_v.view(-1, *self.idx_v.shape[1:])
+
+    def get_kv_buffer(self, layer_id):
+        return self.k, self.v
+
+    def get_index_k_buffer(self, layer_id):
+        return self.idx_k
+
+    def get_index_kv_buffer(self, layer_id):
+        return self.idx_k, self.idx_v
+
+
+def _backend(req_to_token, pool, with_value):
+    b = MiniMaxSparseAttnBackend.__new__(MiniMaxSparseAttnBackend)
+    b.is_npu = False
+    b._linear_verify = True
+    b.speculative_num_draft_tokens = NDT
+    b.max_context_len = MAX_CONTEXT
+    b.req_to_token = req_to_token
+    b.kv_pool = pool
+    b.page_size = PAGE
+    b.block_size_k, b.topk_blocks = BLK, TOPK
+    b.init_blocks, b.local_blocks = INIT_BLOCKS, LOCAL_BLOCKS
+    b.score_type = "max"
+    b.disable_value_layer_ids = set() if with_value else {LAYER_ID}
+    b.use_dense_sparse_decode = False
+    # MSA decode on (no plan is built for verify): verify rows must still run on Triton.
+    b._use_msa_decode, b._msa_owns_decode = True, False
+    b._msa_dec_meta = None
+    b.fp8_attn_gemm = False
+    b.index_cache_enabled = False
+    b._decode_topk_buf = {}
+    b._topk_is_source = {}
+    b.hisparse_coordinator = None
+    b.indexer_cp = None
+    b._linear_verify_meta = None
+    b._prefill_seqblock_meta = None
+    b._max_seqlen_q = b._max_seqlen_k = 1
+    return b
+
+
+_LAYER = SimpleNamespace(
+    layer_id=LAYER_ID,
+    q_scale_float=None,
+    k_scale_float=None,
+    v_scale_float=None,
+    idx_q_scale_float=None,
+    idx_k_scale_float=None,
+    idx_v_scale_float=None,
+)
+
+
+class _Case:
+    def __init__(self, prefixes, with_value, seed=0):
+        torch.manual_seed(seed)
+        self.with_value = with_value
+        self.bs = len(prefixes)
+        self.prefix = torch.tensor(prefixes, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        self.req_to_token, num_pages = _paged_req_to_token(self.bs)
+        self.pool = _Pool(*_caches(num_pages * PAGE, with_value))
+        rows = self.bs * NDT
+        self.q = torch.randn(rows, NQH, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        self.k = torch.randn(rows, NKH, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        self.v = torch.randn_like(self.k)
+        self.idx_q = torch.randn(rows, NIH, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        self.idx_k = torch.randn(rows, 1, HD, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+        self.idx_v = torch.randn_like(self.idx_k) if with_value else None
+        caches = [self.pool.k, self.pool.v, self.pool.idx_k, self.pool.idx_v]
+        for r, p in enumerate(prefixes):
+            slots = self.req_to_token[r, :p].long()
+            for cache in caches:
+                if cache is not None:
+                    cache[slots] = torch.randn(
+                        p, *cache.shape[1:], dtype=cache.dtype, device="cuda"
+                    )
+        draft_pos = self.prefix[:, None] + torch.arange(NDT, device="cuda")
+        self.out_cache_loc = (
+            self.req_to_token.gather(1, draft_pos).reshape(-1).to(torch.int64)
+        )
+
+    def batch(self):
+        return SimpleNamespace(
+            forward_mode=ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY,
+            seq_lens=self.prefix.clone(),
+            seq_lens_cpu=self.prefix.cpu(),
+            req_pool_indices=torch.arange(self.bs, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"),
+            out_cache_loc=self.out_cache_loc.clone(),
+            extend_seq_lens=None,
+            extend_seq_lens_cpu=None,
+            extend_prefix_lens=None,
+            minimax_m3_precached_sparse_layers=None,
+        )
+
+    def reference(self):
+        """Decode every draft row alone, on a copy that ends at its own token."""
+        rows = self.bs * NDT
+        ref_r2t, num_pages = _paged_req_to_token(rows)
+        k, v, idx_k, idx_v = _caches(num_pages * PAGE, self.with_value)
+        pairs = [
+            (k, self.pool.k, self.k),
+            (v, self.pool.v, self.v),
+            (idx_k, self.pool.idx_k, self.idx_k),
+            (idx_v, self.pool.idx_v, self.idx_v),
+        ]
+        seq_lens = []
+        for r in range(self.bs):
+            p = int(self.prefix[r])
+            for j in range(NDT):
+                row = r * NDT + j
+                dst_prefix = ref_r2t[row, :p].long()
+                dst_draft = ref_r2t[row, p : p + j + 1].long()
+                src = self.req_to_token[r, :p].long()
+                for dst, pool_cache, draft in pairs:
+                    if dst is None:
+                        continue
+                    dst[dst_prefix] = pool_cache[src]
+                    dst[dst_draft] = draft[r * NDT : row + 1].view(-1, *dst.shape[1:])
+                seq_lens.append(p + j + 1)
+        seq_lens = torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        idx_o, o = minimax_sparse_decode(
+            self.q,
+            None,
+            k,
+            v,
+            self.idx_q,
+            None,
+            idx_k,
+            idx_v,
+            ref_r2t,
+            torch.arange(rows, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"),
+            seq_lens,
+            int(seq_lens.max()),
+            1,
+            BLK,
+            TOPK,
+            INIT_BLOCKS,
+            LOCAL_BLOCKS,
+            score_type="max",
+            disable_index_value=not self.with_value,
+            page_size=PAGE,
+        )
+        return (
+            None if idx_o is None else idx_o.reshape(rows, -1),
+            o.reshape(rows, -1),
+        )
+
+
+def _verify(backend, batch, q, k, v, idx_q, idx_k, idx_v):
+    backend.init_forward_metadata_in_graph(batch)
+    return backend.forward_extend(
+        q, k, v, _LAYER, batch, idx_q=idx_q, idx_k=idx_k, idx_v=idx_v
+    )
+
+
+def _assert_same(got, want, exact, rows=None):
+    for g, w in zip(got, want):
+        if w is None:
+            assert g is None
+            continue
+        assert not torch.isnan(g).any()
+        if rows is not None:
+            g, w = g[rows], w[rows]
+        if exact:
+            assert torch.equal(g, w)
+        else:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(g, w, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_value", [False, True])
+def test_eager_verify_matches_causal_rows(with_value):
+    """Rows of one request share its cache yet see only their own prefix."""
+    # 5118 + ndt crosses into a new 128-token block, so the bound must count the drafts.
+    case = _Case([1000, 5118], with_value)
+    backend = _backend(case.req_to_token, case.pool, with_value)
+    batch = case.batch()
+    backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph(batch)
+    assert backend._max_seqlen_k == 5118 + NDT
+    got = _verify(
+        backend,
+        batch,
+        case.q,
+        case.k,
+        case.v,
+        case.idx_q,
+        case.idx_k,
+        case.idx_v,
+    )
+    _assert_same(got, case.reference(), exact=True)
+    # Verify leaves the batch's per-request metadata to the dense layers.
+    assert batch.seq_lens.tolist() == [1000, 5118]
+    assert batch.extend_seq_lens is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_value", [False, True])
+def test_graph_replay_at_longer_context(with_value):
+    """A graph captured on 1-token dummies replays at the end of the context."""
+    # Request 0's last two rows run past MAX_CONTEXT: they are clamped, never committed.
+    case = _Case([MAX_CONTEXT - 2, 33000], with_value)
+    backend = _backend(case.req_to_token, case.pool, with_value)
+
+    static = case.batch()
+    static.seq_lens.fill_(1)  # get_cuda_graph_seq_len_fill_value()
+    static.seq_lens_cpu = static.seq_lens.cpu()
+    # Capture-time KV writes land in the free tail of each row.
+    static.out_cache_loc.copy_(
+        case.req_to_token[:, WIDTH - NDT :].reshape(-1).to(torch.int64)
+    )
+    inputs = [t.clone() for t in (case.q, case.k, case.v, case.idx_q, case.idx_k)]
+    inputs.append(None if case.idx_v is None else case.idx_v.clone())
+
+    backend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph(static, in_capture=True)
+    assert backend._max_seqlen_k == MAX_CONTEXT
+    _verify(backend, static, *inputs)  # warm-up: autotune and JIT compile
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        out = _verify(backend, static, *inputs)
+
+    static.seq_lens.copy_(case.prefix)
+    static.out_cache_loc.copy_(case.out_cache_loc)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    # No row may read past the context-length bound the score buffer was sized for.
+    assert int(backend._linear_verify_meta.seq_lens.max()) == MAX_CONTEXT
+    inside = [
+        r
+        for r in range(case.bs * NDT)
+        if int(case.prefix[r // NDT]) + r % NDT + 1 <= MAX_CONTEXT
+    ]
+    # The captured and reference score buffers differ in width; compare to tolerance.
+    _assert_same(out, case.reference(), exact=False, rows=inside)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v"]))

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: Medium**

**Issue**

This line turns on linear verify for CUDA, where the M3 cookbook documents HiSparse. `validate_hisparse` allows HiSparse with `--speculative-eagle-topk 1`, so HiSparse + EAGLE3 now starts. Verify then calls `swap_in_selected_blocks` with `bs * ndt` rows. But `num_real_reqs` holds `batch_size`, and `load_cache_to_device_buffer_kernel` writes `-1` for every row at or past it.

**Example**

With bs=2 and ndt=4, rows 2-7 get no KV slots. The `ndt` rows of one request also update the same `lru_slots[rid]` at the same time. And `top_k_device_locs_buffer` has only one row per request slot.

**Fix**

Raise `NotImplementedError` here when `self.hisparse_coordinator is not None` and speculative decoding is on, until the swap-in handles verify rows.

[by Claude Code] **Severity: functional | Confidence: High**

**Issue**

`_init_linear_verify_metadata` now reads `self.max_context_len` for the clamp. This test builds the backend with `__new__` and never sets that attribute. So `test_verify_keeps_original_batch_and_cache_locations` and `test_graph_replay_reads_new_prefixes_and_requests` now fail with `AttributeError: 'MiniMaxSparseAttnBackend' object has no attribute 'max_context_len'`. I reproduced the error on CPU by replaying this `setUp` and calling `_init_linear_verify_metadata`.

**Fix**

Set a bound above the largest row in the test, for example `self.backend.max_context_len = 8192` next to `_linear_verify`.

**Issue**

With this change, verify rows no longer reach MSA or the prefill metadata. The startup guard at lines 298-309 still says MSA + spec + CUDA graph fails because "TARGET_VERIFY batches route to forward_extend, dereferencing absent extend metadata". That is no longer true after this PR. The guard still makes Blackwell EAGLE3 users set `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA=1`, which also turns off MSA for prefill.

**Fix**

Update the comment to give the reason the guard is still needed. If no reason remains, drop the guard so MSA can serve prefill with EAGLE3.
